Date : 06/04/2026
 Oral Judgment
This is an Appeal under Section 54 of the Land 2 14) Fa 957-2011-J.odt Acquisition Act, 1894 (for
short, 'L.A.Act') by the Acquiring Body against the judgment and award dated 01/09/2010 passed by
the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Amravati (for short, 'Reference Court') in Land
Vidarbha Irrigation Development ... vs Bhimrao Champatrao Deshmukh And 2 ... on 6 April, 2026
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148728311/
1

Reference/L.A.C. No. 109/1997,

2. Heard the learned counsel for the Appellant- Acquiring Body, the learned counsel for the
Claimant and the learned Agp for the State.
Perused the papers on record.

3. The Claimant's land admeasuring 1 H 60 R, 75 R, 90 R and 2 H 31 R, total admeasuring 5H 56
Hr, out of Survey nos. 8/2, 8/3, 8/4 & 7/2 at village Yerli, Tq. Tiwsa, District Amravati came to be
acquired for submergence in Lower Wardha Project.

The Notification under Section 4 of the L.A. Act
was published on 17/02/1994 and the Special Land Acquisition Officer (Slao) declared the award
on 13/12/1996, determining the compensation for lands between Rs. 35,000/- and Rs. 38,500/- per
hectare and for trees Rs. 1920/- per tree. Being not satisfied with the compensation determined by
the Slao, the Claimant filed the above referred Reference for enhancement in the compensation.

Considering the evidence available on record, the learned Reference Court enhanced the
compensation towards 3 14) Fa 957-2011-J.odt lands for Rs. 60,500/- per hectare and for the fruit
bearing trees Rs. 1176/- per tree.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Acquiring Body that, the enhanced compensation by
the learned Reference Court was on higher side.

According to the learned counsel for the Claimant,
the learned Reference Court had appropriately considered the evidence on record and granted the
compensation.

The learned Agp for the State submits that, after considering the material on record,
appropriate order be passed.
5.

Towards lands, the Slao determined the compensation between Rs. 35,000/- and Rs. 38,500/-
per hectare, which came to be enhanced by the learned Reference Court @ Rs. 60,500/- per hectare.

The enhancement by the learned Reference Court is within four (4) times of the rate determined by
the Slao.

There is no dispute that, the State Government has come up with the Policy Decision vide
Government Resolution (Gr) dated 03/11/2016 and Corrigendum dated 23/02/2017 not to
challenge the award wherein the compensation is within four (4) times.

Thus, the challenge towards
enhancement for the lands would not survive.

As regards the compensation towards fruit bearing trees is concerned, the learned Reference
Court

by considering 40% deduction in the rate calculated by the Valuer at Rs. 1,960/- per tree,
determined the per fruit bearing tree rate of Rs. 1176/-.

The said consideration by the learned
Reference Court for the compensation towards fruit bearing trees appears reasonable.

The
compensation determined by the learned Reference Court cannot be said to be exorbitant.

I find no
merits in the Appeal.
Hence, the following order:-

Order
i) The Appeal stands dismissed with no order as to costs.
